overall: The AG found no violation on the complaint's core claim that the Board noticed an executive session to discourage attendance, but independently found violations for an improper Purpose 1 discussion, missing Purpose 2 statement, missing reconvene announcement, non-roll-call vote, and late minutes approval.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair knew the Purpose 1 subject would request open session but the topic was still noticed for executive session to discourage public attendance.
allegations.key_passage: Instead, the Board noticed the topic to be discussed in executive session under Purpose 1 because the Chair intended to hold the discussion in executive session, unless the subject of the discussion appeared and requested otherwise.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a plan existed to adjourn executive session and reconvene in open session to discourage attendance; the AG found no such plan was carried out.
allegations.key_passage: We note first that the alleged plan to adjourn the executive session and reconvene in open session did not occur; the Board posted notice for an executive session and indeed held its discussion in executive session.

allegations.summary: AG independently found the Purpose 1 executive session discussed the police chief's job performance, which is professional competence, not an allowed executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: The entire Purpose 1 executive session discussion concerned the professional competence and performance of the Chief of Police, and thus should not have been held in executive session.

allegations.summary: AG independently found the Chair did not state Purpose 2 before the Board discussed the police chief's reappointment in executive session.
AG independently found the Chair did not announce whether the Board would reconvene in open session after executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We also note that the Chair did not announce whether the Board would reconvene in open session and that the vote to enter into executive session was not taken by roll call.

allegations.summary: AG independently found the vote to enter executive session was not taken by roll call, calling on each member individually.
allegations.key_passage: We also note that the Chair did not announce whether the Board would reconvene in open session and that the vote to enter into executive session was not taken by roll call.

allegations.summary: AG independently found the December 17 executive session minutes were not approved until October 28, 2019, well beyond the timely-approval window.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, the Board did not approve executive session minutes for its December 17 meeting until October 28, 2019, well outside of the three meetings or 30 days allowed for under the Open Meeting Law and its regulations.

allegations.summary: Raised only in a request for further review: that town counsel lacked authority to respond for the Board and that an administrative secretary helped prepare the response.
allegations.key_passage: We do not address these allegations as they were not raised in the original complaint.
